stemBlocks.value: Shape T has vertices (2, 1), (5, 1), (5, 3) and (4, 3); its image Q has vertices (1, 2), (1, 5), (3, 5) and (3, 4). (i) Describe fully the single transformation that maps T onto Q. (ii) On the diagram, draw the image of T after a translation by the vector (-1, 6) and label it M.
Think first: Every vertex of Q is a vertex of T with its two coordinates swapped, which is the signature of one particular mirror line.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p263-q10 from workbook page 263.

solutionSteps.instruction: Read the vertices of T and Q from the grid.

contentBlocks.value: Go round each shape in the same sense.

solutionSteps.instruction: Pair the corresponding vertices and compare the coordinates.
Check the orientation and name the transformation.

contentBlocks.value: Going round T the vertices run anticlockwise but round Q they run clockwise, so the orientation is reversed, which rules out a rotation and confirms a reflection. The rule (x, y) -> (y, x) is reflection in the line y = x.
Result: Reflection in the line y = x

solutionSteps.instruction: For part (ii), apply the translation vector (-1, 6) to each vertex of T.
Plot those four points, join them in the same order as T, and label the shape M.

contentBlocks.value: M sits 1 square left and 6 squares up from T, congruent and the same way up.
Result: Shape M drawn near the top of the grid

strategyBlocks.value: Match the corresponding vertices of T and Q to spot the coordinate rule, name the mirror line, then apply the given vector to each vertex of T for part (ii).

finalAnswerBlocks.value: (i) A reflection in the line y = x.  (ii) M has vertices (1, 7), (4, 7), (4, 9) and (3, 9).

whyThisWorks.value: Reflection in y = x interchanges the roles of the two axes, so a point a units along and b units up becomes b units along and a units up. Because a reflection reverses the sense in which the vertices are traced, checking orientation is a quick way to distinguish a reflection from a rotation when the two could otherwise be confused. The translation in part (ii) leaves both size and orientation alone, so it only shifts the coordinates.

commonErrors.misconception: Calling the mapping a rotation of 90 degrees, which would preserve orientation rather than reverse it.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Calling the mapping a rotation of 90 degrees, which would preserve orientation rather than reverse it.

commonErrors.misconception: Writing the mirror line as y = -x instead of y = x.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Writing the mirror line as y = -x instead of y = x.

commonErrors.misconception: Adding 1 instead of subtracting it for the -1 in the translation vector.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Adding 1 instead of subtracting it for the -1 in the translation vector.

examTip.value: The coordinate rules are worth memorising: reflection in y = x gives (y, x), reflection in y = -x gives (-y, -x), rotation of 90 degrees anticlockwise about O gives (-y, x).
